title: NFR-002 fail-closed: an unavailable audit store blocks the mutation instead of dropping the record
risk: When the audit store is down the system keeps trading and simply loses the audit rows, so external effects exist that the platform cannot account for.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
The audit writer is scripted to fail with a connection error for the duration of the outage window.

steps.action: Send while the audit store is available
steps.expected: The message is delivered once and the audit row is committed.

steps.action: Take the audit store down and attempt a second send
steps.expected: The send is blocked before dispatch with a fail-closed error naming the audit dependency; the adapter counter does not advance.

steps.action: Inspect the interim state and then restore the audit store
steps.expected: No effect exists without an audit row; after restoration a retry with the same effect_key delivers once and writes the audit row.

steps.action: Reconcile adapter effects against audit rows
steps.expected: Effects and audit rows match exactly (2 effects, 2 rows) with no orphan external action.

assertions: While auditing is unavailable, zero external effects occur - the mutation is blocked rather than unlogged.
The block is explicit and typed, not a silent drop of the audit write.
After restoration the retry is idempotent: exactly one new effect for the retried action.
Post-run reconciliation shows a 1:1 mapping between external effects and audit rows.
forbidden: Buffering audit writes in memory and losing them on failure.
Proceeding with the mutation and logging a warning.
Treating the retry as a duplicate and refusing to deliver anything at all.
evidence: Adapter counter log across the three phases.
Fail-closed error record naming the audit dependency.
Reconciliation table of effects versus audit rows.
cleanup: Delete gov- rows after export and restore the audit writer script.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state. The outage is injected at the audit client boundary, so the platform's real fail-closed decision is what is measured.
